column1: # What CI is allowed to cost, and why.
# Format: constant<TAB>value    (seconds, decimal, no units in the value)
# Beside check-owners.tsv because it is the same kind of fact: that table says
# where CI runs a check, this one says how long CI may take to run them all.
# Both are declared here and read out of here, never restated in a workflow.
# Readers: scripts/scope-selftest.py --matrix, which divides `max_shards` by
# the share of faults a run re-proves (#112), or takes `develop_shards` for a
# push to the integration branch (#326); verify.sh's `report_wall_clock`,
# which prints every run against `wall_clock_seconds`; and
# scripts/check-ci-coverage.py, which refuses a file that declares either one
# missing. NOTHING FAILS A RUN
# ON THESE NUMBERS. A slow gate is not a wrong gate, and a budget that can fail
# a build is a budget somebody raises rather than meets. What they buy is that
# the overrun is in the log of the run that caused it.
# --- the budget ---
# A seat that waits on CI comes back to a COLD PREFIX if the wait outlasts its
# provider's prompt-cache TTL, and then pays the whole prefill again at cold
# rates. The TTL is ~30 minutes on first-party Anthropic and ~5 minutes on
# Bedrock, so five minutes is the shortest any seat on this repository runs on
# and is therefore the ceiling: past it, somebody is paying for the runners not
# being tuned. It is a WALL CLOCK, not a sum of runner-minutes -- those are
# unbilled on this repository and are the currency this budget spends.
# Ruled on #87 (2026-09-19), against a run that took 7m27s.
wall_clock_seconds
# --- the ceiling on the shard count ---
# The account runs 20 concurrent jobs. Past that a shard does not start until
# something finishes, so the wall clock stops falling and starts queueing, and
# a count that did not know it would keep splitting.
# 20, the real number, not a number shaded down to leave headroom for
# `verify.yml`'s diet, pages and repo jobs: reserving margin here is a second
# budget nobody declared, competing with the one this file exists to be.
# Nothing balances shards by cost any more (#112): if twenty does not get the
# slowest shard under `wall_clock_seconds`, that is an UNMET BUDGET, and an
# unmet budget is disclosed, not faked by a shard count
# the account cannot actually run concurrently -- `report_wall_clock` prints
# the achieved wall-clock against this budget on every run. The next lever
# past shard count -- per-shard build time -- is its own item, outside #87's
# scope by #87's own text.
max_shards
# --- the ceiling on a superseding run ---
# A push to the integration branch runs the full selftest and is cancelled by
# the next push (#326): it is background, not a gate, and its census is what
# pull requests are scoped against once it completes. It runs on fewer shards
# than `max_shards` so that pull-request runs keep room under the account's 20
# concurrent jobs while it runs. A pull request into the release branch, a
# push to it and the nightly still get `max_shards`. Read by
# scripts/scope-selftest.py --matrix --kind superseding.
# Ruled on #326 (8 to start).
develop_shards
